sentences.text: This creature could grow to a length of 5.2 meters and a mass of 136 kilograms. Its neck vertebrae feature prominent crests above and below, along with an additional pair of cavities not seen in Liliensternus. Derived theropod traits include a spherical joint at the front of the neck and tail vertebrae, plus a vertical ridge on the ilium.
It stands among the rare dinosaurs that might have endured the Triassic-Jurassic extinction event, which wiped out at least half of known species.

Teeth attributed to this animal were unearthed in 2024 in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, representing the first dinosaur remains found there. The original fossils came from the Moon-Airel Formation in Normandy, France, collected by Pareyn in 1959 from sandstone and limestone deposits. A partial skeleton from the Triassic-Jurassic boundary was first described in 1966 as Halticosaurus sp. The holotype at the University of Caen contains a tooth, five cervical vertebrae, two dorsal vertebrae, four sacral vertebrae, tail vertebrae, portions of all pelvic bones, and an unidentified fragment. In 1993, Gilles Cuny and Peter Galton reinterpreted the specimen as a new species of Liliensternus named L. airelensis. Researchers noted differences between L. airelensis and the type species L. liliensterni, leading Ezcurra and Cuny to assign it to the new genus Lophostropheus in 2007.
Lophostropheus is one of the few dinosaurs known to have lived during the Triassic-Jurassic boundary.

The animal is classified within the theropod superfamily Coelophysoidea and belongs to the parent group Coelophysoidea. A 2017 analysis placed Lophostropheus phylogenetically close to the derived theropods Sinosaurus and Cryolophosaurus. It is more closely related to coelophysids, including Coelophysis, than to Liliensternus. Lophostropheus is included in a clade that excludes Coelophysis and Zupaysaurus. Finally, it is classified within the class Reptilia.

The specimen was collected in 1959 from sediments deposited at the Rhaetian-Hettangian boundary, approximately 201 to 200 million years ago. Lophostropheus lived from the Rhaetian to the Hettangian, between 205.7 and 199.5 million years ago.
